text: Benny bought the same ten-dollar burrito twice. Cash, then card.
Same burrito. Same price. So who secretly paid extra?
Not me. I'm a genius.
Round one: cash. Ten bucks. The shop keeps all ten.
Round two: card. Beep.
Before the shop sees a penny, the banks bite off about twenty-four cents.
Twenty-four cents for a beep?!
That's the swipe fee: about two point three six percent.
Some shops even add up to three percent on top.
My burrito has a cover charge?
At MIT, people bid on Celtics tickets. Card payers bid more than double.
Double?! That's two burritos!
Cards make spending hurt less. Carry a balance? About twenty-two percent a year.
Now my burrito has a payment plan!
So who secretly paid extra? Here's the twist.
Shops raise prices for everyone to cover card fees. Even the cash guy.
A Boston Fed study found cash payers help fund card rewards.
So the cash guy... paid for my cashback?
Pay your card in full, and you win. Don't, and the bank wins. Twice.
Cash or card: which makes you spend more? Comment below.
